claims.text: The scheduled pickup was 07:30:00 and the record's own deadline is 07:35:00, five minutes later, yet the trip record reports arrived_by_deadline false and arrived_at null: the driver had not reached the pickup by that deadline. Under POL-NS-24 the rider may then cancel at no charge and any fee charged is refunded in full, so the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee on the fare ledger must be returned in full to the rider, which under POL-GEN-03 is FULL_REFUND of the whole contested amount with no driver compensation.

The driver-device trace is clean and complete - 50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 s, admissibility weight 1.0 - and it never corroborates arrival: the derived arrival check against the 50 m STANDARD-zone radius records corroborated false and nearest_fix null, and the trace ends with the driver stationary at 0 km/h from 07:33:10 all the way through the 07:37:40 cancellation. On POL-NS-21's arrival test the driver was not at the pickup, which is exactly the fact POL-NS-24's no-show refund rests on.

POL-NS-21 runs the 300 s free wait from the driver's arrival, and on this record arrived_at is null, so no free wait ever began. A driver who never started a free wait cannot have had any no-show entitlement mature against a rider who was still waiting past 07:35.

POL-NS-22 charges the 5.00 SGD fee only where the driver cancels after the free wait. Here the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER with reason code RIDER_CANCELLED and no driver cancellation, and the fare ledger shows the 5.00 SGD charged to the rider with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and payment_status CHARGED. The clause that fixes the 5.00 SGD figure therefore does not authorise this charge, and the amount should be returned.

No traffic-data record was attached for this trip: EV-ADVIS-05055-01 is MISSING, carries issue MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, and under POL-GEN-02(3) a MISSING artifact carries no fact. The driver's 'jam at Sembawang Road' (EV-CHAT-05055, MSG-05055-001, repeated in the counterparty statement) is therefore uncorroborated, and POL-NS-24 gives the driver's arrival deadline no traffic exception in any event.

The rider does not press POL-NS-23: the record shows a driver message at 07:31:10 and an answered 40-second in-app call at 07:33:20, both before the 07:37:40 cancellation, so on this record the contact obligation was met. That concession does not rescue the fee, because POL-NS-24's refund turns on the missed arrival deadline, not on contact.

Nothing this ruling needs is missing, so POL-GEN-26 is not engaged and the case can be decided rather than held: the missed deadline is on the trip record, the driver's own chat at 07:36:30 says 'Still jam, sorry' - his own words confirming he was not at the pickup - and the trace never corroborates arrival. The absence of an arrival event here is a positive finding, not an unestablishable fact.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is fully satisfied, so the fee cannot be voided on that ground. The trip record's in-app call log shows a call placed by the driver at 07:33:20, answered and lasting 40 s; the chat log shows driver messages at 07:31:10 and 07:36:30. Both the message limb and the call limb were therefore in place before the 07:37:40 cancellation, and POL-NS-23's remedy — voiding the fee and refunding the rider in full — is not triggered. No FULL_REFUND can rest on the contact ground.

The amount charged is exactly the no-show fee the policy fixes, so there is nothing for a refund to correct. The payments ledger shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD and total_charged of 5.00, and the derived money block confirms fee_matches_policy true against a policy_fee_sgd of 5.00 with refund_already_issued_sgd of 0.00. Where a no-show fee stands, POL-NS-22 makes it the driver's compensation for the time and fuel already spent on the trip.

Even on POL-NS-24's own terms the rider's recovery is capped at the fee and no more. The clause adds a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit only where the driver 'also failed to attempt contact'; here the driver both messaged the rider (MSG-05055-001, read at 07:31:18) and placed an answered 40 s in-app call at 07:33:20, so the goodwill limb is not engaged and adds nothing to the rider's claim.

The cancellation is the rider's own act. The record's reason code is RIDER_CANCELLED, the rider's message at 07:35:00 gives her motive (she was 'going to be late for work'), and her own claim says she 'cancelled and booked another car'. The record shows a driver who was still en route and in contact with her throughout, so the filer's assertion that 'the driver was the one who was late' does not make out a case to disturb the present state, in which the charge stands and 0.00 has been refunded. Under POL-GEN-03 the correct outcome for a rider-filed dispute whose claim is not supported is NO_ACTION, which preserves that payment state.

If the case is not decided on the driver's contact compliance, the record does not settle the one fact that separates a driver stranded by the road from a driver who abandoned the booking. The GPS trace shows 2.448 km of continuous movement toward the pickup before the driver came to a halt at 07:33:10 and stayed stationary to the cancellation — consistent with the congestion he reported twice in the chat log (07:31:10 and 07:36:30). The only artifact that could test that explanation, the traffic advisory, is MISSING: EV-ADVIS-05055-01 carries no payload and a weight_multiplier of 0.0 on the MISSING_ARTIFACT issue, so the congestion can be neither confirmed nor refuted. Under POL-GEN-26 a fact the record cannot establish goes to a human reviewer, and on an escalation the fee is held rather than refunded.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is a NO_SHOW_CHARGE dispute over the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged when the rider cancelled trip TRP-05055 at 07:37:40. The rider is owed that fee back.

The decisive rule is POL-NS-24 (Driver no-show). The trip was scheduled for 07:30:00, so under POL-NS-24 the driver had to be at the pickup by 07:35:00 ('the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes'). He was not. The platform trip record (EV-TRIP-05055, weight 1.0) reports arrived_at null and arrived_by_deadline false, and the clean driver-device GPS trace (EV-GPS-05055, 50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 s, weight 1.0) never places him inside the 50 m STANDARD-zone arrival radius: the arrival check records corroborated false and nearest_fix null, and the trace shows him stationary from 07:33:10 through the 07:37:40 cancellation about 1.1 km short of the pickup. Because the driver failed to arrive by the deadline, the rider was entitled to cancel at no charge, and any fee charged is refunded in full. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-05055) shows the single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD and total_charged of 5.00, with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Amount returned: 5.00 SGD, with no driver compensation. Outcome for the filing party (rider): FULL_REFUND of the whole 5.00 SGD contested.

On the driver's arguments. (1) POL-NS-23 (contact obligation): I accept that the driver messaged the rider at 07:31:10 and placed an answered 40-second in-app call at 07:33:20, both before the 07:37:40 cancellation, so the fee is not voided on the contact ground. That argument succeeds but does not save the charge, because the refund here rests on POL-NS-24, not POL-NS-23. (2) POL-NS-22: I accept the amount charged is exactly the policy fee of 5.00 SGD and that the ledger reconciles (fee_matches_policy true, refund_already_issued_sgd 0.00). But POL-NS-22 charges the fee only when the DRIVER cancels after a free wait. Here the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER with reason code RIDER_CANCELLED, and no free wait ever began: arrived_at is null, so POL-NS-21's 300 s clock, which runs from the driver's arrival, never started. On this record the charge was never authorised. (3) POL-GEN-26 (escalation): I reject it. The fact this refund needs — that the driver had not reached the pickup by 07:35 — is established, not unestablishable, by both the trip record and the GPS trace. The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05055-01, MISSING, MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) does not block the decision: POL-NS-24 gives the arrival deadline no traffic exception, and under POL-GEN-02(3) a missing artifact carries no fact either way, so the reported congestion can neither excuse the missed deadline nor be relied on. (4) The 5.00 SGD goodwill limb of POL-NS-24 is not engaged, because that limb requires the driver to have ALSO failed to attempt contact, and he attempted it twice; nothing is added to the refund on that account.

On the rider's arguments, which carry the case: POL-NS-24 is the ground for the full refund; POL-NS-21 confirms no free wait ever matured because arrived_at is null; POL-NS-22's authorisation point is correct because the driver did not cancel; and the missing traffic record does not create an open question for escalation.

No referral fires. POL-NS-25's repeat no-show counter (rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d) is not present in the rider profile (which records no_show_disputes_30d 0 and prior_no_show_flags 1, neither of which is the field the clause names), so that flag is not triggered. The fee charged is the fixed 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's other-amount referral is not triggered. Confidence is 0.95; the deciding fact is carried by artifacts of weight 1.0, and the dispute value of 5.00 SGD sits below POL-GEN-22's first band, where POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final.

The rider's claim succeeds and the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee (EV-FARE-05055, cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is refunded in full.

The booking was scheduled for 07:30:00. POL-NS-24 lets the driver until 07:35:00 to reach the pickup and gives the rider a no-charge cancellation if he does not. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05055) reports arrived_at null and arrived_by_deadline false, and the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05055, 50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 s, admissibility weight 1.0) shows the driver stationary from 07:33:10 all the way to the 07:37:40 cancellation at a point roughly 1.1 km from the pickup, never inside the 50 m STANDARD-zone arrival radius (arrival_check.corroborated false, nearest_fix null). The driver never arrived by the deadline, so when the rider cancelled at 07:37:40 she was exercising POL-NS-24's no-charge cancellation, and the whole 5.00 SGD must go back to her. Two independent artifacts of full weight carry that fact, so confidence is not reduced by any impairment.

To the driver: your contact was in order. The chat message at 07:31:10 (MSG-05055-001) and the answered 40-second in-app call at 07:33:20 satisfy POL-NS-23, and that claim is accepted - the fee is not voided on the contact ground, and the POL-NS-24 goodwill credit is not engaged because you did attempt contact. Your POL-NS-22 point that 5.00 SGD matches the policy fee is also correct, but the clause does not authorise this charge: it applies where the driver cancels after the free wait, and here the rider cancelled and no free wait ever began, because POL-NS-21 runs the 300 s wait from the driver's arrival and arrived_at is null. Your POL-GEN-26 escalation argument is rejected: the fact the ruling needs - whether you reached the pickup by 07:35:00 - is established by the trip record and the trace, so there is nothing unestablishable to send to a human reviewer. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05055-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) could only speak to why you were held up; POL-NS-24 gives the arrival deadline no traffic exception, so its absence does not change the outcome.

No referral arises. POL-NS-25 does not fire because the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d field, and in any event the fee does not stand; the POL-NS-22 fee-amount check does not fire because the amount charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD the policy fixes. Outcome under POL-GEN-03: the rider is owed the whole contested 5.00 SGD, so this is FULL_REFUND with amount_sgd 5.00 and no driver compensation.

For the rider: the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-05055 is refunded in full. POL-NS-24 lets a rider cancel at no charge when the driver has not reached the pickup by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes, and the whole fee is then refunded. Your pickup was scheduled for 07:30 (trip record EV-TRIP-05055), so the deadline was 07:35, and that record reports arrived_by_deadline false with arrived_at null. The driver-device GPS trace EV-GPS-05055 (weight 1.0; 50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 s) never places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (arrival check corroborated false, nearest_fix null) and shows him stopped roughly 1.1 km from the pickup from 07:33:10 through your 07:37:40 cancellation, matching your account that he was still more than 1 km away. The missed deadline is therefore established, and the fare ledger EV-FARE-05055 (total_charged 5.00) is corrected by returning that 5.00. Because the fee is voided, POL-NS-21's free wait never matured - arrived_at is null, so the 300 s wait could not begin - and POL-NS-22, which fixes the 5.00 SGD figure only where the driver cancels after the free wait, does not authorise a charge where the rider cancelled and the driver never arrived.

For the driver: I accept your contact defence. You messaged at 07:31:10 and placed an answered 40-second in-app call at 07:33:20 (EV-TRIP-05055, EV-CHAT-05055), both before the 07:37:40 cancellation, so POL-NS-23 does not void the fee for lack of contact, and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 arises, because that credit applies only where you also failed to attempt contact. I have not escalated under POL-GEN-26: the fact POL-NS-24 turns on - whether you reached the pickup by 07:35 - is established by the record, and POL-NS-24 contains no exception for traffic. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05055-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) leaves your congestion explanation unconfirmed, but a rule that does not turn on traffic cannot be changed by it, so no fact needed for this ruling is unestablishable. Nor does the amount matching the standard 5.00 SGD fee by itself make the charge lawful: the fee stands only where the no-show entitlement matured, and here it did not. Confidence rests on the trip record and the GPS trace, both at weight 1.0; the dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 band, so under POL-NS-26 this ruling is final.
